To find the **greatest common divisor (GCD)** of the three numbers $ 3339 $, $ 2961 $, and $ 1491 $, we can use the **Euclidean algorithm**, which is an efficient method for computing the GCD of two numbers, and we can extend it to multiple numbers by iteratively computing the GCD of the result with the next number.

---

### Step 1: Compute GCD of 3339 and 2961

Using the Euclidean algorithm:

$$
\begin{align*}
3339 \div 2961 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 378 \\
2961 \div 378 &= 7 \text{ remainder } 315 \\
378 \div 315 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 63 \\
315 \div 63 &= 5 \text{ remainder } 0 \\
\end{align*}
$$

So, $ \gcd(3339, 2961) = 63 $.

---

### Step 2: Compute GCD of 63 and 1491

$$
\begin{align*}
1491 \div 63 &= 23 \text{ remainder } 42 \\
63 \div 42 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 21 \\
42 \div 21 &= 2 \text{ remainder } 0 \\
\end{align*}
$$

So, $ \gcd(63, 1491) = 21 $.

---

### Final Result

Therefore, the **greatest common divisor** of $ 3339 $, $ 2961 $, and $ 1491 $ is:

$$
\boxed{21}
$$
